slides.title: Not every sidewalk lid is equal
slides.sub: Handhole materials, sizes and load tiers

slides.title: Pick the wrong handhole and a truck cracks it.
slides.body: Material, size and load tier all follow from what could drive over it.

slides.title: Three jobs in one box
slides.body: Holds splice closures where cables branch, stores slack loops for re-entry, and breaks long duct runs into pull points.

slides.title: Four materials you'll meet
slides.body: Polymer concrete for sidewalks. Fiberglass for corrosive soil. HDPE for lawns only. Precast concrete under roadways.

slides.title: Road lanes need H-20
slides.body: SCTE 77 tiers are for off-roadway spots. In a travelled lane, use precast concrete with an H-20 rated frame and cover.

slides.title: Same box, other names
slides.body: India often builds RCC or brick chambers on site. Australia calls it a pit, in numbered sizes.

slides.title: Save this for your next underground design

caption:
That rectangular lid in the sidewalk has a load rating, and picking the wrong one gets expensive.

Handholes come in polymer concrete, fiberglass, HDPE and precast concrete, and ANSI/SCTE 77 tiers run from 5,000 lb for lawns to 22,500 lb for driveways. Swipe for the full table and where H-20 takes over.
